title: A Star Flash 50,000 Light Years Away Lit Up Earth's Sky

scenes.text: A dead star's flash lit up Earth's atmosphere.
On December 27, 2004, a magnetar fired a flare from fifty thousand light years away.
The flash lasted about a tenth of a second.
In that blink, it released more energy than our Sun gives off in 150,000 years.
It was bright enough to bounce off the Moon and light up Earth's upper atmosphere.
A tenth of a second, from the other side of the galaxy.

description:
A magnetar called SGR 1806-20 fired a giant flare in December 2004 that lit up Earth's upper atmosphere from about 50,000 light years away.
In a tenth of a second it released more energy than the Sun in 150,000 years.
What's the most powerful thing you can imagine?
thumbnail_text: A STAR FLASH LIT UP OUR SKY
first_comment: If it happened within ten light years, it could have severely damaged our atmosphere. Lucky we're far away!
